newsitem.title: INDIA: P&O unit awarded India port project - paper.
newsitem.headline: P&O unit awarded India port project - paper.

text.p: P&O Australia Ports Pty Ltd, a unit of British multinational Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co, has won a tender for a one billion dollar project to develop a port in the western Indian state of Maharashtra, an Indian newspaper reported on Sunday.
The Financial Express said Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda will handover a letter of intent to P&O Australia at the start of a two-day conference called "Advantage Maharashtra."
The project involves building a port at Vadhvan, north of Bombay, with 29 berths and annual cargo handling capacity of 200 million tonnes.
The newspaper said the project was awarded on a build-own-operate-transfer basis, with a tenure of 30 years. It said P&O will have an option to extend its tenure by a further 20 years.

Maharashtra transport commissioner Rajiv Sinha said the P&O plan envisaged building a port with a dredged draft of 15 metres, plus tide, making it the deepest port on India's west coast, according to the newspaper.
He said it will be able to handle large size crude oil and product carriers and fifth generation container carriers.
Nine berths would be constructed in the first phase of the project involving an investment of 1,080 ($300 million).
